rows.title: No Rate Limiting on Bulk Import Allows Unlimited Note Creation
rows.description: NoteShare's bulk import feature doesn't seem to enforce a rate limit, allowing users on free plans to bypass the 5 live note restriction by importing more notes than the limit of individual note creation.
steps: Create or obtain an account on a free plan.
Prepare a JSON file with more than 5 notes.
Use the POST /notes/import endpoint to import the notes in bulk.
Verify that more than 5 notes are successfully imported, bypassing the plan limit.

rows.title: Excessive Note Sharing without Authentication
rows.description: Users can excessively share notes via the public link feature without needing to authenticate, bypassing organizational boundaries and potentially causing service degradation.
steps: Create a note as a user within Org A on the free plan.
Use POST /notes/{id}/link to generate a public share link.
Distribute this link widely on social media or through a botnet to maximize access.
Repeat the process with multiple notes, circumventing the 5-note limit on the free plan.
Observe NoteShare's service degradation due to increased access requests.

rows.title: Bulk Import Bypass with Continuous Rotation
rows.description: The bulk import feature allows importing up to five notes via the /notes/import endpoint, which is aligned with the free plan limit. However, by deleting existing notes immediately after import and then uploading new ones, a user can continuously rotate notes to maintain access to a larger amount of notes than allowed by the plan restrictions.
steps: Use the /notes/import endpoint to bulk import up to five notes.
Access and use the imported notes as needed.
Delete one or more of the current notes via the DELETE /notes/{id} endpoint to make space.
Repeat the import process with new notes.
Continue the cycle of import, use, delete, and re-import to maintain a large, dynamic set of notes without upgrading the plan.

rows.title: Exceed Free Plan Limit with Bulk Import
rows.description: The Free plan users are limited to at most 5 live notes, but the system allows for bulk importing notes without checking the note count limit first, potentially allowing users to bypass the limit unintentionally or intentionally.
steps: Register a free plan account on NoteShare.
Create a few notes manually to approach the plan limit (e.g., 4 notes).
Use the bulk import feature to import more notes (e.g., 3 additional notes).
Observe that the number of live notes exceeds the allowed limit without receiving a 402 error.

rows.title: Bulk Note Import Without Proper Input Sanitization
rows.description: The bulk note import feature allows for multiple notes to be created in one action without proper input sanitization, which might allow injection of malicious content into the system.
steps: Prepare a JSON payload for the /notes/import endpoint with notes containing script tags or harmful scripts in the 'title' and 'body' fields.
Send the payload using POST /notes/import to bulk-create the malicious notes.
Observe if the injected scripts execute when accessed via GET /notes/{id} in the notes interface.
Exploit these notes within orgs to create confusion or disrupt normal operations.
Continue injecting more notes to maintain a persistent disruptive presence.

rows.title: Insecure Public Note Access via Token Leakage
rows.description: NoteShare's public link sharing allows any anonymous user to access a note via a tokenized URL without authentication. If these URLs are exposed or guessed, sensitive note data could be accessed by unauthorized individuals.
steps: Owner of a note creates a public link via POST /notes/{id}/link.
A token is generated and appended to the URL (e.g., /s/{token}).
An attacker obtains the URL, potentially through user error or network interception.
Attacker accesses the note using GET /s/{token}, bypassing authentication.

rows.title: Public Token Predictability
rows.description: There's a risk that the tokens generated for public links aren't generated with sufficient entropy, making them predictable. If someone can predict the token, they can gain unauthorized access to a note, even if not shared publicly.
steps: Observe multiple /s/{token} URLs generated over time.
Analyze the structure of the tokens for patterns.
Develop a script to generate and test possible tokens based on observed patterns.
Access a note without the owner explicitly creating a public link for you.
rows.error: translator said it cannot be tested

rows.title: Public Share Link Not Revoked on Note Deletion
rows.description: When a note owner deletes a note, the public share link remains active. This allows anyone with the link to continue accessing the note, despite the owner's intention to remove it.
steps: Create a new note in NoteShare.
Generate a public share link for the note.
Share the link with someone outside your organization.
Delete the note intending to restrict access.
Access the note using the public share link, which remains active.

rows.title: Supply Chain Risk via Insecure Third-Party Integration
rows.description: The bulk note import feature allows for integration with other tools without rigorous validation of incoming data. This flaw can enable injection of malicious content from third-party sources, compromising data integrity and potentially introducing vulnerabilities across multiple tenant systems.
steps: Identify a third-party tool that integrates with NoteShare's bulk import feature.
Craft malicious payloads disguising them as legitimate notes.
Use the third-party tool to import these malicious payloads into NoteShare via the /notes/import endpoint.
Observe the injection of malicious content and any effects on data integrity or system behavior.
Repeat the imports across different tenant accounts to exploit multi-system spread.

rows.title: Persistent Note Access via Undeleted Public Links
rows.description: Due to architectural oversight, NoteShare's public links remain active even after notes are deleted, allowing unauthorized and persistent access to potentially sensitive content.
steps: Create a note as an owner and generate a public share link using POST /notes/{id}/link.
Delete the note using DELETE /notes/{id}, expecting to remove access.
Share the public link extensively or monitor access logs to observe continued access despite note deletion.
Leverage access to flood the environment with misleading information via unexpired links.

rows.title: Token Recycling on Public Link Revoking Unleashes UX Chaos
rows.description: By exploiting the lack of state management for public link tokens, a user can continually generate and revoke public share links for the same note without the links truly becoming inactive. This disrupts the user experience by creating confusion over what's shared or not, while potentially overloading the system as users think they're securing their content.
steps: Create a note as a user within Org A on the free plan.
Use POST /notes/{id}/link to generate a public share link.
Immediately POST /notes/{id}/unshare_all to revoke the link.
Repeat the link creation and revocation process rapidly.
Note remains nominally private while public traffic spikes due to unrevoked tokens circulating.

rows.title: Token Reuse Between Deleted and Shared Notes
rows.description: NoteShare fails to properly handle token invalidation for public links when a note is deleted and then re-imported. This reuse of tokens potentially allows previously authorized parties to access the new note if they still possess the old token, highlighting improper link management and execution of distinct operations.
steps: Create a note in Org A and generate a public link with POST /notes/{id}/link.
Delete the note using DELETE /notes/{id}, observing that public access should be revoked.
Re-import the same note content using /notes/import and observe if the link token remains valid for the new note.
Access the note with the previously obtained token using GET /s/{token}.
Confirm that the deleted note's public token can access the newly re-imported note.

rows.title: Error Handling Oversight During Bulk Deletion Impacts System Stability
rows.description: NoteShare's lack of robust error handling when deleting notes in bulk leads to system instability. This can be triggered by crafting a sequence of requests that delete notes repeatedly while others are accessing them, causing service disruption and leaving orphaned references in system databases.
steps: Bulk import multiple notes using the POST /notes/import endpoint.
Generate public share links for each imported note using POST /notes/{id}/link.
Simultaneously trigger multiple GET /s/{token} access requests to these public links.
Initiate repeated DELETE /notes/{id} requests in quick succession targeting the same notes.
Observe the degradation in system performance or any unexpected behaviors like partial deletions or inaccessible notes.

rows.title: Infinite Note Duplication via Autocomplete Glitch
rows.description: By leveraging an unintentional loop between the autocomplete feature and note creation endpoint, a user can perpetually create duplicate notes, bypassing the free plan's note limit and stressing NoteShare's resources.
steps: Create a note using POST /notes with specific content designed to trigger the autocomplete feature.
Use an automated script to rapidly trigger the autocomplete functionality alongside calling POST /notes/import to initiate duplicate note creation.
Continuously loop this sequence, exploiting the lack of rate limits and duplicate checks within the system.
Monitor as NoteShare's system attempts to handle the massive influx of duplicate notes, leading to response delays and potential service interruptions.
Scale the attack by coordinating similar actions across multiple free accounts.
rows.error: translator said it cannot be tested

rows.title: Orchestrated Token Bloat for System Overwhelm
rows.description: By leveraging the ability to generate infinite public share tokens without maintaining an active authentication state, a malicious user can create a multitude of valid links, causing chaos and multiplying system requests beyond manageable levels.
steps: Create a note using a free plan account.
Call POST /notes/{id}/link repetitively to generate numerous public share tokens for this note.
Systematically distribute these tokens across various public platforms and networks.
Monitor the system as the excessive authenticated requests flood the service, leading to potential degradation or unavailability.
Repeat the process with multiple notes to compound the effect.

rows.title: Inadequate Authentication for Public Share Links
rows.description: The notes can be accessed by anyone with a public share link without authentication, risking exposure of sensitive data if the links are guessed or leaked.
steps: Generate and share a public link for a note.
Access the note by using the link without any authentication.

rows.title: Potential for Excessive Data Exposure to Admins
rows.description: Admins within an organization can access any note within that organization, which may lead to exposure of notes that should be restricted to certain users.
steps: Admin logs in to the application.
Access any note using GET /admin/notes/{id} API endpoint, regardless of the note owner’s permission.

rows.title: Cross-Tenant Data Access
rows.description: The system may not have adequate controls to prevent users from different organizations accessing unauthorized data.
steps: Log in as an admin of Org A.
Attempt to access a note using GET /notes/{id} endpoint from Org B or via other non-intended APIs.

rows.title: Denial of Service via Note Creation
rows.description: Excessive note creation through the /notes endpoint can lead to an overwhelming number of requests that degrade system performance.
steps: Continuously send POST requests to the /notes endpoint.
Maximize quota usage and attempt further creation to cause denial by server resources.

rows.title: Improper Handling of Bulk Import Limits
rows.description: The POST /notes/import endpoint does not clearly specify limits per import session, potentially leading to system strain or bypassing tenant restrictions.
steps: Package an excessive number of notes in a single bulk import request.
Submit the request and observe resource strain or unintended allowance of notes beyond user plan limits.

rows.title: Insufficient JSON Token Protection
rows.description: The lack of robust verification for JSON tokens in public share links might make them susceptible to brute force attacks.
steps: Obtain a public share link for a note.
Attempt to programmatically guess valid tokens using a brute force script.

rows.title: Lack of Rate Limiting on Share/Unshare Operations
rows.description: No apparent rate limiting on using share and unshare operations could be abused to flood recipient notifications.
steps: Use POST /notes/{id}/share or POST /notes/{id}/unshare_all to repeatedly share/unshare a note with a user rapidly.
Observe potential notification spam to the recipient.

rows.title: Role Escalation via Poor Access Control
rows.description: The API does not enforce strict access control checks, potentially allowing unauthorized actions via parameter tampering.
steps: Log in as a regular organization user.
Attempt to perform admin-like actions by altering parameters in API requests, such as changing user roles or permission levels.

rows.title: Unvalidated Actions on Notes
rows.description: Actions on notes, like editing and deletion, potentially lack validation to confirm change legitimacy, making them vulnerable to unauthorized exposure.
steps: Craft a well-formed PUT or DELETE API request, altering the target note IDs iteratively.
Observe whether notes you do not own are modified or deleted.

rows.title: Lack of Logging for Public Access
rows.description: There is no mention of logging access to notes via public links, potentially impacting forensic investigation in case of abuse.
steps: Access a note through a public link as an anonymous visitor.
Check system logs to confirm absence of recorded access.

rows.title: Improper Input Sanitization for Notes
rows.description: Input data for note creation is not adequately sanitized, risking injection attacks like HTML or JavaScript.
steps: Create a note with HTML/JavaScript content in the title or body fields.
Access the note to see if the content is executed, confirming improper sanitization.

rows.title: Revoked Link Re-access via Token Replay
rows.description: Re-access of a revoked public share link might be possible if token invalidation is not properly enforced.
steps: Create a public link for a note.
Revoke the link using POST /notes/{id}/unshare_all.
Attempt to access the note again using the previously obtained public link token.

rows.title: Improper Handling of Large Payloads in Bulk Import
rows.description: Submitting large payloads in bulk import without checks can lead to buffer overflow or performance issues.
steps: Send excessively large data payloads using POST /notes/import.
Observe for system crashes or degradation.

rows.title: Lack of Notification for Revoked Access
rows.description: Users are not notified when their access to a shared note is revoked, leading to ambiguity and potential security slips.
steps: Share a note with a user.
Revoke the note access without the user's knowledge.
Attempt to access the note as the user without any prior notification.

rows.title: Weak Handling of Logout for Anonymous Token Access
rows.description: Once accessed, publicly shared notes may not require login, even when subsequently transitioning between accounts, leaving authenticated sessions susceptible.
steps: Access a note via public link.
Log in to an account from the same session.
Check if additional, cross-account information becomes accessible without further authentication.
